capabilities.rationale: Central navigation and status awareness hub for managing multiple concurrent workers.
capabilities.description: Visual dashboard listing active workers, health status, and pending permission badges.

features.name: Worker Grouping
features.rationale: Reduces visual clutter by organizing workers by logical project context.
features.description: Groups workers by project path and renders manager details inline with owner sessions.

behaviors.rationale: Logical grouping matches developer mental model of project-based sessions.
behaviors.summary: Renders workers grouped by project path with associated managers displayed in the row.
behaviors.detail: Workers are organized into collapsible sections based on their project path. The manager process (ending in '-manager') is associated with its worker and displayed in a dedicated 'mgr' column within the owner's row rather than a separate row.

features.name: State Badging
features.rationale: Quickly identifies worker health and consistency with central repository.
features.description: Displays status indicators for workers and highlights stale sessions relative to the hub.

behaviors.rationale: Enables quick identification of inconsistent worker versions.
behaviors.summary: Shows worker states like busy, idle, offline, and marks stale sessions with a badge.
behaviors.detail: Each worker displays a state badge (busy, waiting, idle, offline) using a standardized ordering. Sessions whose git SHA differs from the hub's current SHA are marked as stale. If the hub SHA is unknown, the latest restarted manager's SHA is used as the reference.

behaviors.rationale: Provides precise version identification beyond semantic versioning.
behaviors.summary: Displays manager and worker versions using git SHA.
behaviors.detail: Worker and manager version columns display semver followed by the relevant git SHA (6-40 hex chars). A '.dirty' marker appears if the working tree contains uncommitted changes. The time of day is appended to the version string.

features.name: Sort Controls
features.rationale: Flexible data organization for different inspection priorities.
features.description: Allows operators to sort roster data by any column with ascending/descending cycling.

behaviors.rationale: Efficient data reorganization without complex filtering tools.
behaviors.summary: Cycles through sort directions when clicking column headers.
behaviors.detail: Clicking a column header sorts by that column. The first click sets ascending order, the second toggles to descending, and the third clears sorting. Available sort columns include name, manager, version, state, cwd, context, and recording toggle.

features.name: Empty State
features.rationale: Guides users to launch a worker when the roster is empty.
features.description: Displays helpful guidance when no workers are connected to the hub.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents confusion when no workers are available.
behaviors.summary: Shows 'No workers connected' with instruction to launch via claude-tm.
behaviors.detail: When no workers are connected, the roster displays an empty state with a title and hint suggesting to launch a worker using 'claude-tm' from any project directory.

features.name: Navigation Bar
features.rationale: Organizes complex functionality into discrete, accessible tabs.
features.description: Provides a persistent sidebar for navigating between worker management, permissions, and system settings.

behaviors.rationale: Enables quick access to different management domains.
behaviors.summary: The sidebar displays the service title, navigates to active tabs, and renders badge counts for pending items.
behaviors.detail: The sidebar renders a brand area with the service title, a main navigation list with labels and optional badges, a spacer, and a bottom section for pinned tabs like Settings. The active tab is highlighted, and badges only render when a count is greater than zero.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures operators always know which version of the hub they are using.
behaviors.summary: The sidebar fetches and displays the current software version from the health endpoint.
behaviors.detail: On component mount, the sidebar fetches the '/health' endpoint and extracts the version string. If successful, it renders the version below the navigation list; on failure, it logs the error but continues to function.

behaviors.rationale: Prioritizes attention to tasks that require immediate action.
behaviors.summary: Badges display pending item counts, hidden when the count is zero or undefined.
behaviors.detail: For each tab, the badge element conditionally renders only if the badge prop is defined and strictly greater than zero. This prevents clutter on tabs with no pending actions.

features.name: Worker Listing
features.rationale: Helps operators manage multiple concurrent sessions efficiently.
features.description: Displays a roster of active workers with status indicators.

behaviors.rationale: Provides situational awareness for fleet management.
behaviors.summary: The dashboard enumerates all known workers and their current state.
behaviors.detail: Each entry shows name, last activity timestamp, busy/idle status, and recording toggle state.

features.name: Fleet Health Dashboard
features.rationale: Enables quick identification of failed nodes.
features.description: Displays the current state and connectivity status of all managed worker nodes.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains accurate real-time fleet visibility.
behaviors.summary: Updates the list of workers to reflect current connection status.
behaviors.detail: The dashboard continuously polls or listens for heartbeats from worker nodes. It updates the visual indicator for each worker to show 'Connected', 'Disconnected', or 'Restarting'. It also highlights any pending permission requests with a distinct marker.

features.name: Session Roster
features.rationale: Operators need immediate visibility of fleet state.
features.description: Visual dashboard listing active workers, health status, and pending permission requests.

behaviors.rationale: Provides fleet status at a glance.
behaviors.summary: Lists active workers with health indicators and pending approval counts.
behaviors.detail: The roster displays a list of running worker sessions, showing their names, current health status, and a badge count of permissions awaiting operator approval. It updates automatically when the hub state changes via SSE events.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures real-time visibility of infrastructure changes.
behaviors.summary: Updates roster state automatically on hub events.
behaviors.detail: When the hub emits an SSE event indicating a change in worker state or hub redeployment, the roster list and health badges are refreshed automatically without requiring a page reload. If the hub cannot fetch its git SHA, the roster falls back to a 'freshest-restart' heuristic.

behaviors.rationale: Gives the operator visibility into all managed sessions.
behaviors.summary: Retrieves a snapshot of all registered workers with their current state.
behaviors.detail: Returns a JSON list of all known worker names and their current operational state (e.g., idle, busy, crashed). Automatically filters out 'zombie' entries from workers that crashed without re-registering, as they cannot respond to new requests.

behaviors.rationale: Allows operators to declutter the roster of terminated workers.
behaviors.summary: Permanently removes a worker entry from the hub registry.
behaviors.detail: Accepts a worker name and deletes the corresponding registry entry. This corresponds to the MCP tool `tm_purge_worker`, typically used to clean up the roster via the web UI after a worker is intentionally terminated or becomes permanently unresponsive.

behaviors.rationale: Restores manager functionality without requiring a full worker restart.
behaviors.summary: Re-executes a worker's manager process if it is idle or explicitly forced.
behaviors.detail: Dispatches a command to re-exec a worker's `tubemail.manager` process. If the worker is not in an idle state, the request fails unless a `force` flag is provided. This supports the UI flow where an operator clicks 'Update manager' after a silent overlay initialization.

capabilities.name: Terminal Integration
capabilities.rationale: Provides the primary human interface for inspecting and debugging worker sessions.
capabilities.description: Browser-based integrated terminal with real-time bidirectional streaming and control.

features.name: Real-time Streaming
features.rationale: Enables live inspection of worker processes without overhead.
features.description: Establishes a bidirectional WebSocket connection to stream binary terminal output and user keystrokes.

behaviors.rationale: Provides immediate visibility into the worker session.
behaviors.summary: Establishes a WebSocket connection upon user request or auto-connect.
behaviors.detail: The component initiates a WebSocket connection to the designated pty bridge endpoint using a secure ticket. Upon connection, it waits for a control frame specifying terminal dimensions before rendering output to prevent layout race conditions.

behaviors.rationale: Allows remote execution of arbitrary shell commands.
behaviors.summary: Streams keystrokes to the remote worker process.
behaviors.detail: User input captured by the xterm library (via Shift+Arrow for multi-line selection or standard typing) is encoded as binary data and transmitted over the WebSocket. The remote worker executes the commands and returns output which is streamed back to the browser.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures correct output rendering regardless of window size.
behaviors.summary: Syncs terminal dimensions between client and server.
behaviors.detail: Upon connection, the server sends a 'size' control message. The client applies these dimensions to the xterm instance, ensuring the viewport matches the process's canonical rendering size. This prevents truncation of output if the popout window is resized.

behaviors.rationale: Guides users in diagnosing hanging connections.
behaviors.summary: Displays connection status and stale hints.
behaviors.detail: The UI shows a 'Connecting...' overlay until bytes are received. If silence persists for 4 seconds after the initial connection, a hint suggests the manager needs a restart. This distinguishes connection latency from worker silence.

behaviors.rationale: Enables standard text selection workflows in the terminal.
behaviors.summary: Handles secure copy and paste operations.
behaviors.detail: The component supports Ctrl+Shift+C/V shortcuts which work universally. It also attempts to use the Clipboard API for Ctrl+C if the context is secure; otherwise, it falls back to xterm's default SIGINT behavior.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures UI consistency after network interruptions.
behaviors.summary: Manages disconnected states gracefully.
behaviors.detail: If the WebSocket closes unexpectedly, the component sets a disconnected flag and clears the error state (if recoverable) or shows an error message. The user can attempt to reconnect.

features.name: Live Streaming
features.rationale: Enables real-time inspection of remote execution environments.
features.description: Streams real-time output from the remote worker's terminal to the browser via SSE.

behaviors.rationale: Delivers the 'remote desktop' experience for CLI tools.
behaviors.summary: Streams real-time output from a worker's terminal over SSE.
behaviors.detail: Maintains a persistent connection to forward stdout/stderr and input commands to the worker. The stream updates immediately as the worker executes tasks, allowing the operator to see logs, errors, and outputs in real-time.

features.name: Bidirectional Streaming
features.rationale: Enables live debugging and interaction without SSH access.
features.description: Streams terminal output and commands between browser and worker.

behaviors.rationale: Provides immediate visual feedback on worker actions.
behaviors.summary: The UI connects to worker terminals and streams output in real time.
behaviors.detail: Using SSE or WebSocket, the browser receives terminal text and sends commands, rendering them in an integrated terminal view.

behaviors.rationale: Enables interactive control from a centralized dashboard.
behaviors.summary: Operators can send commands directly from the UI to the worker.
behaviors.detail: Command input entered in the browser is transmitted to the worker process for execution.

capabilities.name: HTTP Control Surface
capabilities.rationale: Offers a familiar graphical alternative to raw MCP tools for general users.
capabilities.description: Provides a web-based interface for operators to monitor and control remote sessions.

features.name: Dashboard
features.rationale: Gives operators a single source of truth for the state of their managed fleet.
features.description: Displays a roster of active workers, health status, and pending permission requests.

behaviors.rationale: Enables quick situational awareness of the managed infrastructure.
behaviors.summary: Fetches and renders the current list of workers and their health.
behaviors.detail: The system queries the hub status endpoint and populates the roster view with real-time data.

behaviors.rationale: Prioritizes security-critical tasks for immediate operator action.
behaviors.summary: Displays pending permission requests awaiting approval.
behaviors.detail: The system filters and highlights requests that require human intervention on the dashboard.

features.name: Approval Control
features.rationale: Transforms the hub from a monitoring tool into an active management console.
features.description: Allows users to approve or deny tool access requests directly from the dashboard.

behaviors.rationale: Automates the enforcement of the operator's security decision.
behaviors.summary: Submits an approval decision to the hub backend.
behaviors.detail: The system processes the user's click event and sends the authorization command to the relevant worker.

capabilities.name: Session Status Indicators
capabilities.rationale: Enables quick assessment of worker health at a glance without drilling into logs.
capabilities.description: Displays real-time badges showing worker health states such as idle, busy, waiting, and various offline conditions.

features.name: Active State Display
features.rationale: Distinguishes between ready-to-run and actively executing sessions to prevent scheduling conflicts.
features.description: Shows whether a worker is idle, processing a request, or waiting for permission approval.

behaviors.rationale: Provides immediate visual confirmation of worker readiness.
behaviors.summary: Updates badge icon and label based on worker current state.
behaviors.detail: The badge displays a checkmark for idle workers, a spinning loader for busy workers, and an alert shield when waiting for permissions.

behaviors.rationale: Helps operators understand task duration and potential bottlenecks.
behaviors.summary: Indicates active processing time for busy workers.
behaviors.detail: When a worker is busy, the badge includes a timer showing how long the task has been running since the last inbound request.

behaviors.rationale: Signals to operators that a decision is pending and should be reviewed.
behaviors.summary: Displays permission waiting state.
behaviors.detail: When a worker requests a new permission, the badge changes to show a shield with an alert icon and the label 'waiting'.

features.name: Offline State Distinction
features.rationale: Allows operators to distinguish between recoverable clean exits and unhandled crashes.
features.description: Differentiates between workers that have crashed unexpectedly versus those that exited cleanly.

behaviors.rationale: Indicates the worker stopped intentionally, allowing automatic retry or cleanup.
behaviors.summary: Shows offline-clean state for gracefully stopped workers.
behaviors.detail: If a worker has stopped running but exited cleanly (no crash), the badge displays a dashed circle icon with the label 'exited'.

behaviors.rationale: Indicates an error state requiring investigation or manual intervention.
behaviors.summary: Shows offline state for crashed workers.
behaviors.detail: If a worker is disconnected and did not exit cleanly, the badge displays a solid X icon with the label 'offline'.

capabilities.name: Live Terminal
capabilities.rationale: Provides full visibility into agent thought processes and execution environment.
capabilities.description: Displays real-time bidirectional terminal output from worker sessions with support for session recording toggles.

features.name: Recording Toggle
features.rationale: Creates a tamper-proof history of agent actions without recording the entire session by default.
features.description: Allows operators to start and stop terminal session recordings for audit purposes.

behaviors.rationale: Prepares the session for forensic analysis.
behaviors.summary: Toggles the terminal session recording state on a specific worker.
behaviors.detail: The UI toggles the recording flag for a worker and updates the worker metadata to reflect recording_enabled status.

features.name: Binary Output Delivery
features.rationale: Ensures accurate rendering of terminal content including non-text characters
features.description: Sends raw pty output bytes to all connected clients as binary WebSocket frames

behaviors.rationale: Delivers volatile terminal output to clients as it happens
behaviors.summary: Streams raw terminal bytes to attached clients
behaviors.detail: When the manager writes pty output to the registry, every attached client receives the raw byte data via a binary WebSocket frame.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains accurate state of active connections
behaviors.summary: Handles client connection lifecycle
behaviors.detail: The system tracks attached clients and removes them when they detach, updating the total client count for each worker.

features.name: Control Message Routing
features.rationale: Provides textual updates like size echoes or manager exit notices
features.description: Delivers JSON control messages to clients for feedback and notifications

behaviors.rationale: Conveys metadata and status information to the UI
behaviors.summary: Sends JSON control messages as text frames
behaviors.detail: When the manager sends a control message like a size update or manager exit notice, it is serialized to JSON and sent to clients as a text WebSocket frame.

features.name: Queue Management
features.rationale: Protects clients from memory exhaustion and dropped frames under load
features.description: Manages per-client async queues with size limits and backpressure handling

behaviors.rationale: Prevents queue from blocking and causing system issues
behaviors.summary: Uses bounded queues to limit client memory usage
behaviors.detail: Each client has an async queue with a maximum size of 512 items; when full, new output frames are dropped to prevent blocking.

behaviors.rationale: Allows clients to detect end of stream on error
behaviors.summary: Soft-closes full queues with empty signal
behaviors.detail: When a queue is full and cannot accept new data, it sends an empty byte frame to signal the client to close the connection gracefully.

features.name: Live Terminal
features.rationale: Allows operators to view and interact with worker output directly in the browser.
features.description: Browser-based integrated terminal with real-time bidirectional streaming for inspecting worker sessions.

behaviors.rationale: Enables direct inspection of worker internals.
behaviors.summary: Opens a live streaming terminal for a specific worker session.
behaviors.detail: When an operator clicks on a worker in the roster, a new terminal pane opens displaying the live output from that worker session. The terminal supports bidirectional communication, allowing operators to send commands to the worker process directly from the browser interface.

behaviors.rationale: Provides focused view for extended monitoring.
behaviors.summary: Supports pop-out mode for isolated terminal windows.
behaviors.detail: If the URL contains pop-out parameters, the application renders the terminal pane alone without the sidebar or other chrome. The terminal fills the entire window height, providing a near-native experience for monitoring a specific session.

capabilities.name: Unified Operator Surface
capabilities.rationale: Aggregates all worker management into a single entry point.
capabilities.description: Provides the web interface and APIs for the hub's capabilities.

features.name: API Aggregation
features.rationale: Consolidates remote management traffic into one router.
features.description: Exposes worker and permission endpoints under a single /tubemail prefix.

behaviors.rationale: Enables scalability via path-based worker separation.
behaviors.summary: Route requests to specific worker sub-paths.
behaviors.detail: The /tubemail prefix routes requests to the BridgeEngine. Worker names are path parameters, enabling isolation per session without requiring stateful connections.

capabilities.name: Security Hardening
capabilities.rationale: Implicit safety foundation preventing unauthorized tool calls and ensuring session isolation.
capabilities.description: Backend enforces strict permissions, risk triage, and secure WebSocket ticketing.

features.name: Secret Enforcement
features.rationale: Prevents accidental exposure of worker sessions without authentication.
features.description: Validates that required secret keys are present before starting worker processes.

behaviors.rationale: Enforces mandatory authentication before operation.
behaviors.summary: Refuses to start if the secret key is missing.
behaviors.detail: On startup, the system checks for the presence of the TUBEMAIL_SECRET environment variable. If it is not set, the system logs an error message and exits with code 2. This ensures that no worker process runs without a shared secret to authenticate with the hub.

features.name: Authentication Gate
features.rationale: Prevents unauthorized access to the operator dashboard.
features.description: Enforces bearer token authentication for all operator interface operations.

behaviors.rationale: Enforces access control boundary.
behaviors.summary: Requires valid authentication token before accessing any hub features.
behaviors.detail: The application uses bearer token authentication. If no valid token is present, the user is shown an authentication gate screen. Once authenticated, the token is stored and used for all subsequent API calls. The token is cleared when the user signs out.

features.name: Secure Ticketing
features.rationale: Replaces long-lived credentials with short-lived, scoped access tokens.
features.description: Manages WebSocket connections using secure tickets to prevent unauthorized access.

behaviors.rationale: Protects long-lived credentials from interception.
behaviors.summary: Exchanges a bearer token for a secure WebSocket ticket on first connect.
behaviors.detail: The initial handshake requests a ticket that authorizes subsequent communication without exposing the raw token.

features.name: Loopback Auth
features.rationale: Safely exposes secrets only to same-machine browsers in dev mode.
features.description: Provides a dev bootstrap endpoint that only accepts connections from localhost to expose bearer secrets for local development.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures secrets are not exposed to the public internet.
behaviors.summary: Returns a bearer secret only to requests originating from localhost.
behaviors.detail: The `/dev-bootstrap` endpoint returns the bearer token required by the UI to skip the auth gate. It strictly validates the client host, returning 403 for any non-loopback requests (e.g., 192.168.x.x or external IPs). It also checks for an environment flag to disable this entirely if strict manual paste is required.

features.name: Ticket Issuance
features.rationale: Enables secure, authenticated terminal streaming sessions.
features.description: Issues pty-ticket identifiers necessary for establishing secure WebSocket connections to worker terminals.

behaviors.rationale: Authenticates and encrypts the terminal streaming channel.
behaviors.summary: Generates a pty-ticket for a new terminal streaming session.
behaviors.detail: Accepts a payload defining the terminal request and returns a ticket identifier. This ticket is bound to the authenticated session and is used by the client to open the WebSocket stream to the worker's PTY.

features.name: Bearer Auth Enforcement
features.rationale: Ensures only authorized operators can manage workers.
features.description: Validates Bearer tokens against a shared secret on every request.

behaviors.rationale: Protects the hub from brute force and timing side-channels.
behaviors.summary: Validate Bearer token via constant-time comparison.
behaviors.detail: Extracts the token from the Authorization header or query string. Uses hmac.compare_digest for constant-time comparison to prevent timing attacks. Rejects requests with missing or invalid tokens.

features.name: Path Sanitization
features.rationale: Ensures worker names map safely to filesystem paths.
features.description: Validates worker names in URLs to prevent directory traversal.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents accidental or malicious filesystem escape.
behaviors.summary: Reject worker names with path traversal sequences.
behaviors.detail: Uses a regex to validate worker names allow alphanumeric, spaces, dots, and dashes. Explicitly rejects names containing '..' to prevent escape from the workers directory.

capabilities.name: Persistent Configuration
capabilities.rationale: Ensures safe updates without data loss or partial configurations.
capabilities.description: Manages atomic writes of global hub settings including recording knobs and retention policies to disk.

features.name: Atomic Write
features.rationale: Prevents corruption if the system crashes mid-save.
features.description: Persists configuration changes by writing to a temporary file first, then atomically replacing the original.

behaviors.rationale: Guarantees data consistency during writes.
behaviors.summary: Writes a new configuration file safely by replacing the old one atomically.
behaviors.detail: The system writes the updated configuration to a temporary file with a .tmp extension before replacing the original file. If a crash occurs during the save, the system either retains the previous valid configuration or the new complete file, never a partial state.

features.name: Recording Defaults
features.rationale: Allows centralized control of recording without manual per-worker setup.
features.description: Stores global default flags and limits that control terminal session recording behavior for new workers.

behaviors.rationale: Streamlines setup for consistent audit trails.
behaviors.summary: Applies global recording enablement flags to new workers upon registration.
behaviors.detail: A boolean flag determines if recording starts automatically for new worker sessions. Existing workers retain their individual per-worker settings regardless of this global default. The system respects existing worker configurations while applying defaults only to new registrations.

features.name: Retention Policy
features.rationale: Prevents unbounded disk usage by rotating and deleting old session logs.
features.description: Manages limits on maximum file size and count of recording files before garbage collection occurs.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures bounded disk usage for audit trails.
behaviors.summary: Rotates recording files when size limit is exceeded and limits total file count.
behaviors.detail: The system monitors active recording files and rotates them when they exceed the configured byte limit, typically 5 MiB. Additionally, it enforces a maximum count of retained files (default 4), deleting the oldest files if the count exceeds the limit to maintain bounded storage.

capabilities.name: API Gateway
capabilities.rationale: Standardizes communication protocols to simplify integration with various worker types.
capabilities.description: Exposes a standardized HTTP API to per-worker forwarders for seamless integration.

features.name: Forwarding Endpoint
features.rationale: Acts as a secure entry point for automated worker communication channels.
features.description: Accepts requests from worker forwarders and routes them to the orchestration core.

behaviors.rationale: Enables scalable deployment of workers without manual hub reconfiguration.
behaviors.summary: Accepts connection requests from worker forwarder processes.
behaviors.detail: The system authenticates the forwarder and establishes a connection channel to the hub.

capabilities.name: Message Reliability
capabilities.rationale: Closes gaps in optional reply tool usage by forcing event posting on stop.
capabilities.description: Guarantees that the final assistant response is delivered to the operator dashboard regardless of agent tool invocation patterns.

features.name: Stop Hook Relay
features.rationale: Ensures audit trails remain complete when LLM omits explicit reply calls.
features.description: Automatically forwards the last assistant turn text to the hub upon session stop.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents invisible fence reports by forcing delivery on session stop.
behaviors.summary: Hooks extracts the latest assistant message and posts it to the hub's inbound endpoint upon receiving a Stop event.
behaviors.detail: The hook parses the Stop event payload to extract the conversation transcript or inline messages. It specifically looks for the most recent message with the role 'assistant' and concatenates any text blocks while ignoring tool-use events. The extracted text is then formatted as a new outbound event and sent via HTTP POST to the hub.

behaviors.rationale: Accommodates schema variations across Claude Code versions without failure.
behaviors.summary: Handles Multiple Message Formats Robustly
behaviors.detail: The hook supports parsing inline message arrays within the payload as well as external JSONL transcript files. It attempts to read inline messages first and falls back to the transcript path if present. If neither source yields content, the hook exits gracefully without blocking the stop operation.

behaviors.rationale: Preserves full reasoning context including hidden thinking steps.
behaviors.summary: Conciliates Multi-Block Content
behaviors.detail: When content is provided as a list of blocks, the hook concatenates text and thinking blocks in order while filtering out tool-use and tool-result blocks. Thinking blocks are included to capture full reasoning chains, which is important for audit trails.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures worker termination is never stalled by hub connectivity issues.
behaviors.summary: Operates Best-Effort on Failure
behaviors.detail: The HTTP POST to the hub is executed with a best-effort approach. If the network call fails or the hub is unreachable, the hook logs the error to stderr and exits with status code 0 to ensure the worker stop process never blocks or hangs.

features.name: Activation Guard
features.rationale: Prevents interference with non-tubemail Claude Code sessions.
features.description: Automatically detects if running within a tubemail session to avoid unnecessary execution.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures hooks do not interfere with standard Claude Code usage.
behaviors.summary: Skips execution if the Tubemail worker name is not defined.
behaviors.detail: The hook checks for the presence of the environment variable TM_WORKER_NAME. If this variable is not set, the hook identifies itself as running outside a managed tubemail session and exits immediately without performing any relay actions.

capabilities.name: Session Teardown
capabilities.rationale: Ensures clean exit and resource release on every stop command or crash
capabilities.description: Installs a persistent hook configuration that executes cleanup logic whenever a user session is terminated.

features.name: Stop Hook Installation
features.rationale: Persistent state in user settings ensures the hook survives across restarts
features.description: Writes a 'Stop' hook entry to the user's .claude/settings.json configuration file.

behaviors.rationale: Atomic write prevents corruption of user settings during installation
behaviors.summary: Writes the hook configuration to the user's settings file if it does not already exist.
behaviors.detail: The installer reads ~/.claude/settings.json, constructs a new entry under hooks.Stop, and writes the updated JSON atomically to ensure data integrity. It creates the file only if it already exists.

behaviors.rationale: Idempotency allows safe re-runs on every startup without side effects
behaviors.summary: Skips installation if the hook command is already registered in settings.
behaviors.detail: The installer iterates through existing 'Stop' hook entries and checks if the specified command string matches. If found, it treats the system as installed and returns success without modifying the file.

behaviors.rationale: Environment gating ensures system-specific hooks do not interfere with vanilla usage
behaviors.summary: Ignores sessions not part of the tubemail-channel system.
behaviors.detail: The hook execution logic (handled by the installed post_stop_relay script) checks the TM_WORKER_NAME environment variable. If unset, the hook does nothing, ensuring other Claude sessions are unaffected.

behaviors.rationale: Fail-safe design protects user config from corruption on errors
behaviors.summary: Reports errors when the settings file cannot be read or written.
behaviors.detail: If JSON parsing fails, the file does not exist, or write permissions are denied, the installer logs an error to stderr and returns a failure code without corrupting existing state.

capabilities.name: Secure WebSocket Auth
capabilities.rationale: Enforces secure WebSocket connection with ephemeral credentials to prevent header injection attacks.
capabilities.description: Generates time-bounded tokens allowing anonymous browser sessions to upgrade to authenticated WebSocket connections.

features.name: Ticket Generation
features.rationale: Creates a secure handshake token valid for only 30 seconds to mitigate replay attacks.
features.description: Issues a cryptographically random token tied to a specific worker process and expiration time.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures each connection attempt requires a fresh credential to prevent token reuse.
behaviors.summary: Issuing a new WebSocket authentication ticket for a worker process.
behaviors.detail: The system generates a secure random token and binds it to the worker identifier with a default 30-second expiration window.

features.name: Ticket Consumption
features.rationale: Atomic pop-and-check prevents lateral movement by ensuring single-use scope per worker.
features.description: Validates incoming tokens, consuming the ticket to prevent reuse against the same worker.

behaviors.rationale: Atomic consumption prevents the same ticket from being used multiple times.
behaviors.summary: Consuming a ticket to establish a secure WebSocket connection.
behaviors.detail: The system validates the token, worker scope, and expiration time atomically, marking the ticket as used or expired immediately.

behaviors.rationale: Enforces strict worker boundaries to prevent cross-process privilege escalation.
behaviors.summary: Rejecting a ticket scoped to a different worker.
behaviors.detail: The system detects a ticket intended for another worker and rejects the connection attempt, preventing lateral movement between workers.

features.name: Ticket Lifecycle Management
features.rationale: Automatically removes stale tokens to minimize attack surface and maintain memory efficiency.
features.description: Cleans up expired and unused tickets to maintain system hygiene and prevent log pollution.

behaviors.rationale: Maintains a clean state by removing credentials that are no longer valid.
behaviors.summary: Sweeping expired tickets from the system.
behaviors.detail: The system identifies and removes tickets that have exceeded their expiration time, returning a count of evicted tickets.

features.name: Secure WebSocket Bridge
features.rationale: Prevents interception and ensures keystrokes are never sent over unencrypted connections.
features.description: Establishes a bidirectional channel requiring explicit authentication tokens and TLS enforcement.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents cross-site WebSocket hijacking attacks.
behaviors.summary: Rejects connections originating from unapproved domains.
behaviors.detail: The system validates the request's Origin header against a pre-configured allowlist. If the origin is not in the allowlist, the WebSocket upgrade is refused immediately.

behaviors.rationale: Ensures sensitive keystrokes and terminal data are encrypted in transit.
behaviors.summary: Enforces TLS for keystroke transmission.
behaviors.detail: The system checks for the presence of server certificate files. If TLS is required but the connection is not secure (HTTP), the upgrade is denied.

behaviors.rationale: Limits the lifespan of credentials to a single connection session.
behaviors.summary: Consumes single-use authentication tickets.
behaviors.detail: Upon connection, the server validates a ticket parameter. It marks the ticket as consumed, preventing replay attacks across different sessions.

behaviors.rationale: Delivers a pixel-perfect replica of the worker's terminal output.
behaviors.summary: Streamlines terminal output to the browser.
behaviors.detail: The server reads raw data from the underlying process queue and forwards binary frames containing screen updates to the browser client.

behaviors.rationale: Allows the operator to interact directly with the remote worker's shell.
behaviors.summary: Relays user keystrokes to the worker process.
behaviors.detail: The server receives binary data from the browser and forwards it to the manager engine, which injects the bytes into the worker's terminal stream.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents injection attacks via malformed identifiers.
behaviors.summary: Validates worker names against allowed shapes.
behaviors.detail: Before accepting a connection, the system verifies the worker identifier matches the expected alphanumeric format.

behaviors.rationale: Prevents unauthorized connection attempts.
behaviors.summary: Issues secure tickets to validate operator identity.
behaviors.detail: The system generates time-limited cryptographic tickets for authenticated users. Clients present these tickets when establishing a WebSocket connection. The hub validates the ticket signature and expiration before granting access to control endpoints.
